business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (Crown in right of the United Kingdom; Bermuda is a self-governing British Overseas Territory)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — English Common Law and equity as the bedrock, supplemented by locally enacted statutes (Companies Act 1981, Proceeds of Crime Act 1997) and final appeal to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council; the territory is treated as an offshore special jurisdiction with a distinct tax-exempt corporate regime.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK-US FATCA Intergovernmental Agreement (extended to Bermuda)
UK tax relief practice for Bermuda-resident companies (no comprehensive UK-Bermuda DTA; relief via UK domestic territorial rules)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS membership and Pillar Two implementation (Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 for large MNE groups only)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1981 (as amended) (registered office, registers, incorporation rules); Companies and Limited Liability Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2017 and Beneficial Ownership (Companies and Limited Liability Companies) Amendment Regulations 2018, as amended (mandatory UBO register maintained private and filed with the central register administered under the Financial Intelligence Agency Act 2006); Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 (as amended); Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008 (as amended); Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 (UK, extended to Bermuda) and the International Sanctions Regulations (Bermuda); Economic Substance Act 2018 (relevant activity assessment only).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — statutory beneficial ownership register is not publicly searchable; access is limited to designated competent authorities (Financial Intelligence Agency, Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Monetary Authority, police and tax authorities) in accordance with FATF-compliant access rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws of the proposed exempted company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bermuda notary public (attorney admitted in Bermuda)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille — issued by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (London) pursuant to the UK's extension of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention to Bermuda; consular legalization substitute where apostille route is unavailable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (exempted company) obtained from the Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Legal Affairs and Constitutional Reform
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (UK FCDO Legalisation Office, London) for bank and EMI onboarding; no notarization required for Registrar-issued certificates

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (compliance certificate) for the pre-incorporation due diligence file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (UK FCDO Legalisation Office, London) or consular legalization where the receiving jurisdiction is not party to the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized beneficial ownership declaration and register extract for the proposed exempted company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bermuda notary public and the company's designated corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (UK FCDO Legalisation Office, London); used for bank and financial institution KYC, not for public filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory formation-stage and ongoing screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and material counterparties against HM Treasury Consolidated List (UK sanctions extended to Bermuda), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, and Bermuda International Sanctions Regulations; risk-based enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family and close associates as required by the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008 (as amended) and the FIA AML/ATF Guidance Notes; FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions must be screened and treated with enhanced measures; adverse media and negative-news checks are mandatory for the target payment rails (Stripe Billing and Direct Debit).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies e-Services Portal (Companies Registry, Ministry of Legal Affairs and Constitutional Reform) — online name reservation and incorporation filing system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that corporate names appear in the English/Latin alphabet; no local-script transliteration regime exists in Bermuda; the name of an exempted company must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; names are assessed for distinctiveness, misleading character and undesirability under section 17 of the Companies Act 1981, with 'The' and minor typographic variations disregarded for identity/confusion purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or its Bermuda counsel shall (i) within 14 days of the refusal notification file an administrative appeal letter with the Registrar of Companies requesting reconsideration and attaching a revised Statutory Declaration and, where relevant, consent letters from holders of similar names, trademarks or regulated marks; (ii) if refusal is sustained, submit a formal review request to the Minister responsible for legal affairs under the Companies Act 1981 appealing on grounds of material error or non-applicability of the prohibition; (iii) as final administrative remedy, apply to the Supreme Court of Bermuda for judicial review; parallel to the appeal, a fresh reservation application with a modified name may be filed immediately to avoid delay; legal counsels' engagement is presumed for appeal drafting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual registered office is not permissible — the Companies Act 1981 requires every exempted company to maintain a physical registered office in Bermuda at the premises of a licensed corporate services provider, law firm or accounting firm; remote/professional registered-office arrangements are standard and satisfy the statutory obligation. The substantive software development, ERP/CRM cloud hosting, and customer contracting activity may be carried on entirely outside Bermuda without physical Bermuda staff or premises, subject to Economic Substance Act 2018 assessment (the 'vertical cloud software' business is not itself a relevant activity unless it morphs into intellectual-property holding, financing and leasing, or headquarters business).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: LOW — approximately 3–5% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection for a non-licensed, low-risk exempted company with no regulated activity; probability rises materially (to 25% or more) upon default in beneficial ownership register filings, suspicious activity reporting, or Economic Substance annual filing obligations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1981 (as amended) of Bermuda, Part II (Incorporation, ss.4-24) and Part III (Exempted Companies); Corporate Service Provider Business Act 2000 for licensed registered agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Government of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CM1 (Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company) together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued at par or nil paid, no escrow account or pre-funding deposit is required, and only the authorized share capital schedule and subscriber declarations must be submitted to the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) INITIAL SHARE SUBSCRIPTION — The Board accepts the subscription for 1,000 ordinary shares at US$1.00 each and directs issuance at par value to the initial shareholder. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE — The registered office shall be that of the licensed corporate services provider, as approved by the Directors. (3) OFFICER APPOINTMENTS — [Name] is appointed Chairman, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer of the Company. (4) BANKING — The Chairman and Secretary jointly are authorized to open banking relationships and execute electronic money institution and payment processor mandates. (5) GOVERNANCE — The Company shall adopt the Companies Act 1981 and its Articles as the governing instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Government of Bermuda (online via Companies e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Bermuda Registrar of Companies e-Registry portal and submit the proposed exempted company name. The name must not conflict with an existing registered name nor include prohibited words unless a consent or licence from the relevant supervisory authority is supplied. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a 30-day name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Proposed exempted company name and two alternative names
Name reservation application form (e-Registry)
Consent from relevant supervisory authority where the name contains regulated words such as bank, insurance, trust or re-insurance
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly select a new name variation and resubmit; alternatively, file a written representation to the Registrar and request reconsideration within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Bermuda corporate services provider licensed under the Corporate Service Provider Business Act 2000 to draft the exempted company's Memorandum and Articles. The Memorandum must state the corporate name, registered office address, business objects, and authorized share capital. Each subscriber must execute the Memorandum in the presence of a witness, and the licensed provider endorses the document before submission.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association of an exempted company
Articles of Association adopted for an exempted company
Witnessed subscriber signatures
Consent to act of subscribers or first directors
Licensed corporate service provider's endorsement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal or execution defects and resubmit within five business days; if the Registrar questions the object clause, file a revised Memorandum authorized by special resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the completed Form CM1 for incorporation of an exempted company via the e-Registry portal or in physical form at the Registry General. Attach the executed Memorandum and Articles, the Declaration of Compliance, and the registered agent's consent. Pay the government incorporation fee of approximately USD 2,500 by bank transfer or approved electronic payment method. The Registrar processes the application and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form CM1 (Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and witnessed)
Declaration of Compliance signed by the licensed corporate service provider
Consent of first director(s) and company secretary
Government fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, supply the requested clarification or documentation within five business days; expedited review may be purchased where urgency exists. If the Registry rejects the application, correct the identified deficiency and re-file before the name reservation expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Exempted Status Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review, the Registrar seals and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a separate Certificate of Exempted Company Status. Verify the company number, exact corporate name, and date of incorporation, and collect the original sealed certificates. Where the company will maintain a presence in Bermuda, the registered office confirmation is recorded and, where applicable, a Certificate of Compliance is obtained before trading.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certificate of Exempted Company Status
Registered office confirmation from the Bermuda corporate service provider
Receipt of incorporation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or administrative errors, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction without reprocessing the entire application; material corrections require a court-sanctioned rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Statutory Registers and Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office of the Exempted Company / Board of Directors / Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in person or by written resolution. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving share subscription, adopting the registered office, and appointing officers. Prepare and maintain the register of directors, register of members, register of beneficial owners, and register of charges at the Bermuda registered office. File the beneficial ownership declaration and any notice of the registered agent with the Registrar as required by law.
required_dossiers: First board resolution adopting the board, share subscription, and registered office
Register of Directors and Officers
Register of Shareholders with details of issued shares
Register of Beneficial Owners
Consent to act of each director and officer
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects a beneficial ownership filing, revisit the definition of beneficial owner, obtain proper identification from the ultimate beneficial owner, and re-file online. Settle any late-filing penalty, update the register, and if officer appointments change, file the notice of change within the statutory timeframe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing authority regulates vertical ERP/CRM cloud software under ISIC 6201 in Bermuda.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — the activity falls outside the sectors requiring a licence under the Bermuda Business License Act 1980 (Schedule 3 non-regulated service).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Heritage, Government of Bermuda
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a pure office-based software and cloud service with no physical industrial plant, manufacturing, or discharge; no EIA screening or registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No production-related discharge. Office wastewater and domestic sewage must comply with the Department of Health wastewater discharge guidelines. Standby generator emissions, if installed, must meet the threshold limits of the Bermuda Air Pollution Control Regulations 2009, including particulate matter and NOx emissions limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service together with a structural load assessment and workplace clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1982; office occupancy must be certified prior to employee deployment. No civil defense licence is imposed for cloud-based software activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bermuda Tax Administration under the Office of the Tax Commissioner (Ministry of Finance) – responsible for payroll tax and other local levies. Company registration is handled by the Registrar of Companies. Official portal: www.gov.bm
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Bermuda does not operate a general corporate income tax; hence no standard national TIN or VAT ID is issued. A Bermuda Exempted Company obtains a Company Registration Number (CRN) and a Bermuda Business Number (BBN) from the Registrar of Companies upon incorporation. For payroll tax purposes, the entity must register with the Tax Commissioner as an employer within 15 days of the first payroll payment, obtaining a payroll tax account number. No other tax registration is required for exempted companies deriving income solely from outside Bermuda.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – Bermuda Exempted Companies are non-resident entities, exempt from local income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty on shares. They are subject only to employment-related levies (payroll tax and social insurance contributions). A certificate of tax exemption under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 may guarantee additional exemption from any future Bermuda taxation until 2035 (renewable to 2050).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Bermuda law. The only relevant statutory election is the application for a 'Tax Exemption Certificate' under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act, which locks in the entity's zero-rate direct tax position. Companies may also elect to register for payroll tax as a bundled or general employer, but this does not affect entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None – Bermuda does not levy VAT, GST, or sales and use tax. The closest indirect charges are import customs duties under the Customs Act 2008 and payroll tax (classified as a direct employment levy).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT/GST/sales tax registration threshold exists. For import duty, every importer must obtain a Customs Tariff Classification and file declarations per shipment. For payroll tax, registration is compulsory upon hiring the first employee, regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists for indirect tax. Bermuda Customs uses the ASYCUDA World electronic single-window system for submission of customs declarations and duty assessment. Payroll tax returns are filed electronically through the Office of the Tax Commissioner's online portal. No digital stamping or API-based government clearance is required for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable – Bermuda's indirect tax system has no VAT/GST export zero-rating mechanism. Exported goods are outside the scope of customs duty (duty applies only at importation). Services rendered from Bermuda to foreign clients are not subject to any Bermuda indirect tax. For direct tax purposes, the exempted company's foreign-source income is exempt, and a 'No Tax Liability' letter can be obtained from the Ministry of Finance upon request.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for VAT zero-rating – no such regime exists. For physical exports from Bermuda, the following customs documents are mandatory:
Customs Export Declaration (Bermuda Customs Form C5)
Commercial Invoice (English, detailing export value and description)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (evidence of physical movement out of Bermuda)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export zero-rating fraud or clawback regime exists because there is no applicable indirect tax on exports. Customs misdeclarations in export documentation are subject to penalties under the Customs Act 2008, including fines up to 150% of duty evaded and potential imprisonment. For payroll tax, willful false declarations may attract fines and interest on unpaid amounts. The Tax Commissioner may conduct audits and make retroactive assessments for up to six years in cases of fraudulent or negligent returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA), acting as the central bank, currency board and foreign exchange control authority for the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda, pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1972, the Exchange Control Regulations 1973 and the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969; HM Treasury of the United Kingdom retains concurrent jurisdiction over financial sanctions and the UK Sanctions List applicable to Bermuda as a UK Overseas Territory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermudian dollar (BMD) is pegged at a fixed 1:1 rate to the US dollar (USD), and USD is legal tender and circulates freely throughout Bermuda. The capital account and current account are both fully open for a Bermuda Exempted Company: equity injections, intercompany loans, dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, liquidation proceeds and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders require no prior BMA exchange control approval and are subject to zero withholding tax under Bermuda law. Convertibility is therefore unrestricted in theory and in banking practice; the only substantive hurdle is the account-holding bank's internal credit and AML/CFT due diligence. A deemed-tax-exempt Bermudian company is not taxed on foreign-source income, and profit repatriation to the UK parent or other non-resident shareholders is not conditioned on a tax clearance certificate. Practical remittance friction arises exclusively from source-of-funds/source-of-wealth documentation required by the correspondent banking chain, especially where transactions originate from UK/EU fintech platforms such as Stripe or a UK-authorised Payment Institution. Because Bermuda is an offshore special territory of the United Kingdom and is not a member of the EEA, UK/EU merchant acquiring and Direct Debit rails generally require a UK/EU PSP as intermediary rather than direct BMA-licensed membership in payment schemes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Bermuda imposes no statutory duty to surrender or repatriate export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline for onshore crediting of export receipts. Under the Exchange Control Act 1972 and current BMA practice, a Bermuda Exempted Company may retain foreign currency proceeds (including SaaS subscription receipts, ERP/CRM software licence fees, cloud service revenues and trade receivables) indefinitely in offshore accounts denominated in USD, GBP, EUR or any freely convertible currency. There is no requirement to convert export receipts into BMD; the BMD/USD peg makes conversion economically neutral. Reporting obligations are limited to anti-money-laundering thresholds: the bank must file a suspicious activity report for transactions above BMD 25,000 only where the circumstances are unusual or the counterparty presents ML/TF risk, and the company must maintain underlying commercial documentation (invoices, contracts, merchant settlement statements) for a minimum of five years in accordance with the Proceeds of Crime Regulations 1998 and the BMA AML/ATF Code of Practice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited (Butterfield)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operational Account (USD, GBP, EUR, BMD)
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Corporate Operating Account
Operational Account with integrated online cash management and FX desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. A Bermuda Exempted Company is a legal customer of, but cannot itself be licensed as, a UK/EU Electronic Money Institution; Bermuda has no operational EMII licensing regime and the BMA does not issue PSD2 equivalent licences. For cross-border treasury purposes, the viable structure is to pair a licensed Bermuda commercial bank (Butterfield or HSBC Bermuda) as the master corporate account with an offshore digital EMI such as Wise, Airwallex or Revolut Business acting as a PSP/multi-currency settlement rail for Stripe Billing payouts and SEPA/Bacs Direct Debit collections. The EMI must be regulated under UK PSD2 or an EEA National Bank's EMI regime; it will classify the Bermuda entity as a non-EEA corporate customer and typically requires full KYC, proof of beneficial ownership, and a justification for the Bermuda nexus. Many EMIs decline a wholly Bermuda-based merchant because of perceived substance risk; therefore the recommended onboarding approach is to present the Bermuda Exempted Company as an intermediate holding/IP-licensing company within a UK group with consolidated financial statements. Direct Debit outbound from Bermuda is not permitted on the UK Bacs scheme; Direct Debit collection (company as originator/merchant) is feasible through a UK-authorised PSP that maintains the merchant account, while the PSP remits net settlement in USD/GBP to the Bermuda bank via SWIFT. The BMA expects that all customer-facing payment services and foreign exchange activities carried out with Bermuda clients are performed by licensed institutions; using an unlicensed offshore EMI as a pass-through account is legally sensitive and should be avoided.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or bank-to-bank verified appearance is effectively mandatory for Bermuda bank account opening. Butterfield and HSBC Bermuda require at least one director, the company's registered representative, or a duly authorised signatory to attend an in-person identification interview at a Bermuda branch or at an overseas affiliate through a bank-to-bank 'banker's confirmation' process. Remote opening purely by video call is not accepted as a primary mechanism by Butterfield or HSBC Bermuda; Clarien Bank may permit remote onboarding through an insured digital onboarding portal at its discretion, but only after a video interview and electronic signature. The mandatory KYC evidence bundle comprises: (i) certified true copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws; (ii) a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of Companies; (iii) the register of directors and officers; (iv) the beneficial ownership register filed under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Act 2017; (v) notarised passport copies and proof of residential address for every director, shareholder and 10%+ beneficial owner; (vi) a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds questionnaire; (vii) board resolution authorising the account opening and specifying the authorised signatories; and (viii) if the company is tax-exempt, a copy of the tax exemption certificate issued by the Minister of Finance. Physical attendance can be waived only where a Bermuda-licensed fiduciary or corporate services provider (registered agent) introduces the account and certifies the identity of all signatories under the AML/ATF Code of Practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt domicile flagged as a low-substance ring-fenced structure: the company is a Bermuda Exempted Company with zero Bermuda corporation tax and no obvious operational nexus; the bank's transaction monitoring raises a 'tax evasion typology' red flag where UK parent and EEA customers route subscription revenue into a BMD-peg offshore account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) the Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration or annual economic substance return concluding that the company is a 'pure equity holding entity' or that it conducts core income-generating activities (billing, IP licensing, procurement) with adequate employees and premises in the UK/Bermuda; (ii) a group tax transparency chart evidencing that the company is not using Bermuda to avoid UK corporation tax and not claiming treaty benefit; (iii) UK GAAP consolidated forecast showing actual headcount, board meeting minutes, cloud infrastructure contracts and client agreements in the vertical ERP/CRM segment; (iv) a confirmatory tax opinion that the company has no UK permanent establishment and no UK hidden PE risk; (v) the Minister of Finance Tax Exemption Certificate; and (vi) corporate charters confirming the commercial rationale for the Bermuda legal entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity and non-resident control: the register shows one or more ultimate beneficial owners resident outside the UK/EEA, or shares are held through nominee arrangements, or the capital injection originates from a third party without clear nexus to the UBO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) a complete Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register filed with the Registrar of Companies, fully visible to the bank; (ii) a genealological ownership chart from the entity to each individual UBO (100% chain); (iii) certified passport copies and proof of address for each director, shareholder and UBO holding 10% or more; (iv) a signed source-of-funds declaration with underlying bank statements of the subscribing shareholder; (v) the executed share subscription agreement and share certificate; (vi) a nominee termination letter or declaration of trust if in place; and (vii) the registered agent's certification of identity under the AML/ATF Code of Practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified initial capital injection channelled via a fintech EMI or Stripe merchant settlement during the first 30 days: the bank sees high-volume, low-value non-face-to-face receivables (subscriptions) with no associated commercial contract file, triggering 'rapid movement of funds' and 'layering' typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) a formal capital introduction letter from the parent or subscriber stating the aggregate amount and banking provenance; (ii) the source-of-wealth file for the subscribing shareholder showing at least 12 months of bank statements; (iii) the executed Stripe Merchant Service Agreement and Stripe settlement schedule identifying the Bermuda entity as the merchant of record; (iv) a VAT/GST-compliant sample invoice from the ERP/CRM vertical; (v) a cash-flow model reconciling expected subscription receipts, cloud hosting costs, FX conversion needs and quarterly net income; (vi) the company's privacy policy and terms-of-service stating that the Bermuda entity is the data controller and seller; and (vii) a Director's Certificate confirming that no cash withdrawals, no pass-through to unauthorised third parties, and no layering structures are employed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile mismatch between the declared business and actual clearing behaviour: the account receives USD/EUR/GBP receipts from UK Direct Debit rails and pays out to cloud providers, domain registrars and a UAE/U.S. hosting vendor, while also converting currencies via a foreign EMI rather than the Bermuda account bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) copies of routine contracts with hosting providers, data centres and cloud vendors, including a description of services and country of performance; (ii) a monthly projected FX conversion schedule quantifying future GBP/USD and EUR/USD exposure and confirming that all FX is executed with the licensed Bermuda bank or an approved institution; (iii) a reconciliation ledger showing Stripe payout UETRs and corresponding SWIFT inflows into the Bermuda operating account; (iv) the official merchant of record agreement with the PSP and the Direct Debit originator agreement; (v) the board-approved treasury policy; and (vi) a KYC file for every commercial client above the EUR/GBP 2,000 threshold, documenting the legal name, jurisdiction, etc.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing protocol for equity capital into the Bermuda Exempted Company is a SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022) wire from the subscribing shareholder's own bank account to the company's segregated Capital Escrow Account at Butterfield or HSBC Bermuda. For USD, the wire is cleared through the Bermudian bank's U.S. correspondent (typically Bank of New York Mellon or JPMorgan Chase, New York), using a BOP/transaction narrative of 'share subscription — non-resident direct investment into Bermuda exempted company [registered number, entity ID BM_EXEMPTED_CO]'. For GBP, route via CHAPS or Faster Payments to the Bank of England settlement account of Butterfield's London correspondent and then onward SWIFT to Bermuda; for EUR, use TARGET2 via a eurozone correspondent. The beneficiary bank requires that the Payment Details field identify the company's Bermudian bank account and a purpose code consistent with cross-border equity investment. Inbound share subscriptions are not subject to Bermuda exchange control approval, but the bank will credit an escrow sub-ledger until it receives (i) the board resolution approving the share issue, (ii) the executed subscription agreement, (iii) a statement of source of funds for the electronic transfer, (iv) the updated register of members, and (v) a Director's Certificate confirming the aggregate capital raised. All files must be uploaded to the bank before the escrow is released for investment or operating expenditure. The transaction is reportable to the BMA only if it forms part of a suspicious pattern; otherwise, no regulatory filing is required. The company must record the capital injection in the Bermuda financial statements and file the annual return to the Registrar of Companies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade disbursements is SWIFT MT103 (with a UETR reference) for supplier payments, software royalties, cloud infrastructure and intercompany charges. The Bermuda account bank will execute the payment through its correspondent network, typically same-day USD to U.S. beneficiaries, T+1 for EUR via TARGET2, and T+1 for GBP via CHAPS, with a narrative containing the relevant purpose code (e.g., 'payment for software licence fees' or 'payment for cloud hosting services'). For high-value or conditional transactions, the company may utilise a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Bermuda bank under ICC UCP 600, chiefly for hardware procurement or infrastructure equipment where the vendor requires documentary protection; the expiring bank will be in the vendor's country, and the advising bank must be a reputable institution. For recurring low-value disbursements, the company may aggregate supplier payments and route them through the integrated FX desk of Butterfield or HSBC Bermuda, or through a regulated UK/EU EMI with an API if the Bermuda bank provides correspondent plumbing. Stripe Billing payouts are settled by the merchant bank to the company in GBP/USD/EUR, and the funds are then swept to the Bermuda operational account via SWIFT; there is no direct debit outbound rail from Bermuda. For Bacs Direct Debit collection, the company must act as the creditor (originator) through a UK-authorised PSP, with the PSP collecting from UK customers and remitting the net aggregate to the Bermuda bank account. All outbound payments above GBP 10,000 must carry a clear purpose code and, where the beneficiary is a UK/EU tax resident, appropriate withholding tax certificates where required. The bank will maintain a sanctioned-party screening log and expects the company to maintain underlying invoices and contracts for each payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (vanilla, up to 24 months) quoted in USD, GBP and EUR, executed under a bilateral FX Master Agreement between the Bermuda Exempted Company and the Bermuda account bank; these are the recommended first instrument given the BMD/USD 1:1 peg and the company's GBP/USD subscription/hosting mismatch.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing currencies of the company's emerging-market customer base; permissible for hedging subscription receivables denominated in non-convertible Asian or African currencies, with the payoff settled in USD by the Bermudian bank as a licensed counterparty, and requiring ISDA 2002 documentation and a netting agreement.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/GBP and USD/EUR) converting the currency base of long-dated cloud infrastructure financing and matching expected subscription cash flows; each swap must be evidenced by a confirmation under an ISDA Master Agreement and is subject to the bank's credit limit.

FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for temporary treasury liquidity smoothing, permitted for up to 12 months, and commonly used to bridge timing differences between Stripe settlement dates and vendor payment dates.

Vanilla FX options and flex forwards, permitted at the discretion of the licensed bank, with a board-approved treasury mandate and a signed options addendum; Bermuda imposes no exchange control restriction on the use of derivatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an Exempted Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual return must be certified by the Bermuda resident director or secretary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default fine on the company and every officer in default; continued failure after formal Registrar notice can lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution under the Companies Act 1981

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Accountant General, Ministry of Finance, Bermuda, collected through the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on the anniversary of incorporation, with a 30-day grace period; prorated for the first year at incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic loss of good standing, refusal of certificates of good standing, interest on arrears, and eventual strike-off from the Bermuda Register of Companies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Economic Substance Department, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each financial year; a nil declaration is still mandatory if no relevant activity is carried on
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty of USD 10,000 for failure to file, further enforcement-notice penalties for continuing default, potential strike-off, and reporting to the Bermuda Tax Authority for exchange with foreign jurisdictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Beneficial Ownership Unit, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the company's annual return; any change in beneficial ownership or significant control must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal summary offence for the company and each officer, daily default fines for continuing non-compliance, disqualification proceedings, and administrative strike-off for prolonged default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset or headcount threshold applies to a Bermuda Exempted Company. A statutory independent audit is mandatory for all exempted companies unless the members unanimously resolve in writing to dispense with the appointment of auditors. Audit waiver is never available for licensed, regulated or public companies such as insurers, banks, trust companies, investment businesses, collective investment scheme operators, or entities required by a Bermuda regulator to file audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda does not issue a local GAAP. Exempted companies prepare financial statements under IFRS as issued by the IASB, or under US GAAP where the shareholder resolution and auditor permit. The chosen framework must be consistently applied and retained for information-exchange purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017, the exempted company must maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register at its registered office, identify individuals with 25% or more ownership or control, file initial beneficial ownership particulars with the Registrar, and file any subsequent change within 30 days. At each annual return date, the Bermuda corporate secretary must conduct a full register audit, verify the share transfer records against the member register, and confirm that the beneficial ownership particulars previously filed remain accurate.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500 – US$2,500 per annum for Bermuda registered office, registered agent, resident secretary and routine annual statutory filing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$8,000 – US$18,500 per annum for a non-regulated software and CRM exempted company preparing single-entity IFRS financial statements; higher for consolidated IFRS group audits or regulated-entity audits

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% via the Bermuda Exempted Company regime; a 15% Corporate Income Tax (CIT) applies exclusively to constituent entities of in-scope multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Export/offshore exempted status removes Bermuda income, capital gains, dividend and estate taxes for ordinary commercial income; no statutory tax holidays exist because the headline tax base is nil for out-of-scope entities; payroll tax at up to 10% may apply to Bermuda payroll and customs duties on imports remain payable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT Form 1) e-filed on the Bermuda CIT electronic portal administered by the Commissioner for Corporate Income Tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 months after the fiscal year-end; transitional first-year extension to 18 months for groups newly brought within the GloBE rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, exempted company number, registered office in Bermuda, jurisdiction of ultimate parent and tax identifiers of each constituent entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident constituent entities must list their jurisdiction and ownership percentage but file jointly with the Bermuda filing entity; no foreign tax ID is required if the entity has no tax registration abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GloBE Income and Adjusted Covered Taxes as computed under the OECD GloBE Model Rules, reconciled to financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert amounts to BMD using the fiscal-year closing exchange rate; foreign-controlled constituent entities must use the consolidated group accounting standard of the ultimate parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 — Effective tax rate and top-up tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Yearly ETR per jurisdiction and the Bermuda top-up tax allocation under the Income Inclusion Rule and Undertaxed Profits Rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a foreign parent has allocated top-up tax to a Bermuda constituent entity under the IIR, the amount must be declared and paid even when no tax was assessed locally on ordinary profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal officer's declaration that the return is complete and accurate, signed under the Companies Act 1981 records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The attestation must be given by a director or authorized officer located in Bermuda or by a designated local service provider; knowingly false attestation triggers criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of BMD 500 plus continuing daily penalty of BMD 50, capped at BMD 10,000 per return; understating top-up tax attracts a penalty up to 100% of the tax undercharged; deliberate evasion is an offence punishable by fine up to BMD 10,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Exempted Company Annual Return filed through the Registrar of Companies online e-Services portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 120 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — Registered office and communication details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current registered office in Bermuda, mailing address and principal business address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempted company incorporated by non-residents must retain a licensed Bermuda registered office and update the address before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B — Ownership and governance register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors and officers as recorded in the statutory register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident ownership is allowed; nominee shareholders must disclose the underlying beneficial owner for AML and ESR purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Election to file audited financial statements or to file a waiver of auditing accompanied by the statutory solvency/declaration basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Waiver of audit is lawful for exempted companies; it does not remove the obligation to maintain records and files under the ESR or CIT record-keeping rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Registrar-imposed late filing fees for each default period; repeated non-filing triggers deregistration, automatic dissolution, strike-off and vesting of assets in the Crown; directors can be disqualified from acting in Bermuda.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Annual Declaration (ESR declaration) filed via the Registrar of Companies / Economic Substance e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the entity's fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the relevant activity: holding entity, pure IP business, headquarters, distribution and service centre, or other statutory category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned vertical cloud company must classify itself carefully; providing group ERP/CRM services under contract to a UK parent typically constitutes a headquarters or distribution and service centre activity, whereas licensing proprietary software constitutes pure IP business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time employees in Bermuda, physical premises, quantum of core income generation expenditure and place of senior management decision-making.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Outsourced staff or virtual offices in the UK are disregarded; only persons employed on the Bermuda payroll and physical premises in Bermuda satisfy the test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from the relevant activity, audited or accountant-certified computations, and signed declaration by the local principal officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be accompanied by working papers; HMRC may request the filing from Bermuda under the UK-Bermuda Tax Information Exchange Agreement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: fixed penalty BMD 500; failure to satisfy economic substance: substantial financial penalties from BMD 5,000 up to BMD 250,000 and continuing daily penalties until remediated; persistent breach enables the Registrar to strike off and wind up the company.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Bermuda imposes no dividend withholding tax or capital gains tax on distributions by an Exempted Company to resident or non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No relief protocol is required for Bermuda-source dividends because the statutory WHT is nil. Bermuda has no comprehensive double tax agreement with the UK and only limited DTAs worldwide; the UK-Bermuda TIEA covers information exchange only. An exempted company seeking a tax residence certificate for foreign filings must submit a request to the Registrar of Companies with evidence of central management and control in Bermuda; treaty benefits remain unavailable for UK-source IP royalties because no DTA exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Bermuda-source royalty and interest WHT: 0%; treaty-stipulated rates: N/A as no broad DTA network applies. Caution: when the counterparty is UK-resident, UK WHT of 20% may apply at source to royalty and interest payments flowing to Bermuda, and no UK-Bermuda treaty reduction is available; net payment clauses should be negotiated so the Bermuda entity receives gross contractual amounts.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File documentation applies only to constituent entities of an in-scope multinational group with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more (approximately BMD 810 million at prevailing exchange rates) under the CIT Act 2023; entities below the threshold have no statutory TP documentation duty in Bermuda, although the ESR requires evidence of intra-group pricing for substance reporting.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2018 and accompanying Income Tax Requirements apply to all exempted companies carrying on relevant activities, including holding entities, headquarters, distribution and service centres and IP businesses. A Vertical CRM cloud company that sells or licenses the software to the UK group while managing contracts from Bermuda should characterize its activity as either a distribution and service centre or pure IP business; each requires core income generation activity, senior management in Bermuda, adequate full-time employees, physical premises and core expenditure in Bermuda. A pure equity-holding subsidiary satisfies reduced substance requirements (employees and premises only). Below-threshold exempted companies cannot rely on the absence of CIT to avoid ESR compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and false CIT status declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An in-scope multinational group falsely declaring itself out-of-scope, failing to file the CIT return, concealing GloBE income, or knowingly signing a materially false CIT Form 1 for a Bermuda exempted company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine up to BMD 10,000 on conviction for evasion; civil penalty up to 100% of the undercharged top-up tax plus daily default penalties of BMD 50 per day; the Commissioner may publish the names of defaulting entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly prepare or sign a false return are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of unpaid tax with interest; criminal courts may impose travel restrictions while proceedings are pending and order disqualification from acting as directors in Bermuda.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance (ESR abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Bermuda office and mailbox address for the exempted company while management, staff, core income generation and decision-making occur wholly in the UK, and claiming Bermuda exemption for royalties or service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR penalties starting at BMD 5,000 and reaching BMD 250,000 for substantive default, with continuing daily penalties; the Registrar may strike off and dissolve the company; on dissolution the assets vest in the Crown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly fail to meet the substance test are personally liable for the imposed fines; repeated abuse results in disqualification orders, travel bans under restraint orders in money-laundering-linked substance investigations, and possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing Stripe Billing and Direct Debit payments through the Bermuda entity for third-party merchants without a registered AML compliance programme, failing customer due diligence or economic sanctions screening, or using the exempted company as an unlicensed money transmission conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Regulations: custodial sentence up to 14 years and criminal fines on indictment; The Bermuda Monetary Authority can impose civil monetary penalties, asset freezing orders and revocation of any relevant registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners who knowingly permit laundering are criminally liable in their personal capacity; confiscation orders attach to personal assets; travel bans and extradition requests are routinely issued by the Supreme Court in predicate offshore abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file annual returns and register maintenance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Persistent non-filing of the Exempted Company Annual Return within 120 days of the anniversary, maintaining dead-register officers, or failing to disclose ultimate beneficial owners while continuing to trade through bank accounts in Bermuda.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing financial penalties imposed by the Registrar, automatic strike-off proceedings and dissolution of the company; the protected cell and asset-shielding benefits of the exempted company are lost on dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held insolvency-liable for debts incurred after the strike-off and may be personally ordered to restore company assets; the Register of Corporate Insolvency disqualification applies for up to 5 years in Bermuda.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: UK CFC and diverted profits exposure on the Bermuda vertical cloud structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Bermuda exempted company is managed and controlled from the UK, has no substantive Bermuda staff or premises, and derives the preponderance of its revenue from intra-group software licences and CRM services to UK customers, while UK profits remain parked offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: No additional Bermuda statutory sanction, but the UK parent attracts a CFC charge under TIOPA 2010 Part 9A at 25% on attributable profits and UK Diverted Profits Tax of 25% plus interest and penalties on the UK entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: UK HMRC may issue personal liability notices to directors who facilitated the avoidance, impose time-to-pay refusals and conduct criminal investigations under the UK Fraud Act; mutual legal assistance between the UK and Bermuda permits freezing orders, travel bans and extradition where evasion exceeds the statutory threshold.
